## Summary

A currency can no longer disappear from aequorOS net open position limits or filing evidence merely because its daily FX return history is missing. Its position remains in the facts; missing valuation evidence or an older incomplete run produces a refusal that names the currency. Incomplete historical runs are omitted from dashboard trends.

## What changed

- Split the shared writer: Notice NOP facts and the CAR market-risk FX sums use separate valuation paths. Capital preserves its existing aggregation exactly, including the GHS 6,425 hedge fixture. Capital-side refusal is tracked separately in [the follow-up](https://github.com/CedynGroup/aequorOS/issues/424).
- Retain every currency in the existing on-balance and FX-hedge NOP book. A currency without history requires an ingested current quote; an implied position-book ratio does not substitute for that quote.
- Compare official and live FX facts with accepted canonical positions at the exact source date. Validate stored filing runs against the accepted currency universe and official FX facts before DBK, FX-NOP, BSD13 or BSD1B uses them. Complete older runs remain usable; no blanket version cutoff is imposed.
- Reuse the valuation refusal rules for BSD13 NOP totals, retaining its detailed missing-rate messages for schedules and contract conversions. Unvalued hedge legs remain visible and block the NOP rather than deleting their currency.
- Preserve the explicit disclosure of flat currencies that require no rate. Store their currency names with the run so coverage checks can distinguish them from an omitted exposure.
- Check both selected headlines and stored historical trend runs through the prefetched batch. Omit incomplete historical points while preserving the named refusal on direct selection and a complete newer/current headline, without additional database round trips.
- Batch accepted currency coverage in one scoped, database-deduplicated projection for the trend window. Read only the date, position type, position currency and both FX_HEDGE leg currencies; filter domestic on-balance positions in the database. Preserve exact-date, organization/bank, accepted/warning, superseded and withdrawn predicates without hydrating snapshots, positions, products or counterparties.
- Bump the FX engine to `regulatory-fx-v1.1.0`, document the contract, and shrink three legacy type-error counts.

The NOP-only workbench can use complete valued positions without a return history. The full FX run also supplies historical VaR and stressed VaR, so it refuses with `fx_return_history:<currency>` until history arrives. This preserves the complete analysis contract and avoids inventing a VaR estimate.

## Why

**Basis:** Bank of Ghana Notice BG/FMD/2026/07, in force. [Official Notice](https://www.bog.gov.gh/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/BG-FMD-2026-07-Revised-Directive-on-Foreign-Exchange-FX-PositionLimits-1.pdf).

**Implements:** ¶1(a)–(b), currency coverage for single-currency and aggregate NOP limits; ¶3, complete DBK evidence; the unnumbered NET OPEN POSITION COMPUTATION heading, valuation evidence for a retained currency. Daily return-history availability is a VaR input, not a reason to exclude a currency from the NOP book.

**Not:** a change to the limit formula, long-position prohibition, NOF denominator, contingent-exposure scope, trade reconciliation, filing holidays or regulatory-parameter approval. This change fixes the missing-currency defect; it does not claim complete Notice alignment.

## How it was tested

- **39 focused tests passed** across the hermetic currency-coverage and credit exposure-book modules plus canonical fact derivation, using `UV_PYTHON_DOWNLOADS=never uv run --frozen pytest`. They cover exact-date position loading, accepted-source filtering, no-history currency inclusion and refusal, single historical spots, filing recovery, and the unchanged GHS 6,425 / GHS 12,850 short / GHS 0 capital controls.
- Historical-trend regressions exercise explicit/current headlines, with either accepted positions or official facts supplying the omitted CHF currency. They assert unchanged complete headlines and points, omission of the partial point, and a named refusal on direct selection.
- The compact-projection regression checks eight distinct currency-field rows, domestic filtering, both hedge legs, missing-leg defaults, warning acceptance, pending/superseded/withdrawn exclusions, exact dates, same-organization bank isolation, cross-organization isolation, and zero ORM hydration.
- Five FX dashboard query-shape cases also passed, preserving 17 explicit-mode and 19 current-mode SQL statements, flat trend query growth, one bulk call per resource, and identical output for complete books.
